summary: Transient sidechain heartbeat suppression leading to GPU credit exhaustion and reserved pool lull
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-10T10:45Z NimbleDocs reported progressive throughput degradation on their dedicated pool (tenant: nimbledocs-dedicated-1). P50 remained stable but p95/p99 climbed and many short-stream requests observed timeouts and attach failures. Impact: customer reported increased latency and a 25% drop in successful requests across pinned routes for ~2 hours. Timeline: 10:42Z - first errors in customer traces; 10:45Z - automated alert: allocator-heartbeat-gap > 5s; 10:55Z - autoscaler performed a shrink (reclaimed GPUs); 11:05Z - customer reports repeated retries and elevated 5xxs. This ticket tracks investigation into a transient "heartbeat suppression" pattern originating from a sidecar process that appears to hold prefetch leases and starve the allocator's credit accounting, causing autoscaler reactions and GPU-credit exhaustion.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a dedicated tenant with small, frequent short-streams and prefetch enabled. 2) Simulate sidecar log flood (high stdout/stderr throughput) or introduce a synthetic sidecall that delays connection close by ~2-5s. 3) Observe allocator-heartbeat metrics and prefetch-lease count for the tenant. 4) Watch autoscaler decisions (scale down events) and GPU credit metrics. Expected: allocator keeps leases short; actual: prefetch leases linger and allocator reports heartbeat suppression leading to shrink decisions.

investigation_notes: Observations: - Prefetch lease durations for the affected tenant spiked from median ~30ms to >120s for a small subset of sessions. - Allocator emitted heartbeat_gap events correlated with sidecar stdout/stderr spikes. - Autoscaler policy interpreted sustained heartbeat gaps as underutilization and triggered a shrink window; this reduced available GPUs while leases still held, causing attach failures and a rapid GPU credit drain when remaining GPUs absorbed load. - No kernel or driver errors observed. - Noisy sidecar processes were customer-side components that emit high-volume logs; these logs correlated temporally with lease hold times. Hypothesis: high-volume sidecar I/O caused network/socket backpressure in the sidecar, delaying connection teardown and keeping prefetch leases pinned. The allocator's heartbeat sensor uses a bounded-response heuristic that treats prolonged lease retention as a suppressed heartbeat, which fed the autoscaler shrink decision and ultimately caused GPU-credit exhaustion through repeated retry storms. Tests run: - Reproduced locally by adding a 90s delayed-close to sidecar; observed allocator heartbeat_gap and subsequent autoscaler shrink. - Short-term mitigation (reducing prefetch lease TTL and increasing min-pool-size) prevented immediate shrink in test cluster. Metrics referenced: grafana/dashboard/dedicated/pool-allocator, grafana/dashboard/nimbledocs/prefetch, cloudwatch/nimbledocs/gpu-credit. Current status: root-cause plausible; fix path identified (sidecar backpressure handling + allocator heartbeat sensitivity tweak).
comments: 2026-03-10T11:20Z - Marcus Li (assigned): Thanks Aisha. Reproduced in staging with the synthetic sidecar flood. Narrowed signal to socket-close delays. Creating repro harness and escalating to infra-team.

2026-03-10T12:05Z - Aisha Patel: Applied temporary mitigations for customer: reduced prefetch TTL from 5m -> 5s for nimbledocs tenant and bumped min_reserved_gpus +1. Observed drop in attach timeouts. Customer confirmed improvements in their test routes.

2026-03-10T13:30Z - SRE (Elena Gomez): Looking at allocator config. Proposed change: make heartbeat sensor use median of last N leases rather than single long-held lease to avoid overreacting to outliers. Will open infra PR if mitigation holds.

2026-03-10T14:10Z - Customer (NimbleDocs support): Reported reduced errors after mitigation but asked for permanent fix and an explanation. Shared their sidecar log samples (uploaded to ticket attachments).
resolution: Mitigation implemented: temporary prefetch TTL lowered for the affected tenant and min_reserved_gpus increased to absorb immediate load. Monitoring alerts tuned to ignore single long-held leases. Customer routes returned to acceptable latency and error rates. Permanent fix: infra PR to adjust allocator heartbeat heuristic (use rolling-window median) and a serving-runtime patch to detect and close held prefetch sockets when sidecar backpressure detected. PR drafted: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4821. Status: mitigation in prod; code change pending review and canary.
